x: In the Puranas King Vena (father of Prithu) was the son of King Anga of the line of Dhruva and Sunitha; Sagara and Anshuman belong to the solar line, Kapila is a sage.

s: Among the Sixteen Janapadas, the greatest power was exercised by the following
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Magadha); it is added as option 5.
Magadha became the most powerful of the sixteen Mahajanapadas, absorbing Kosala, Avanti, Vatsa and the rest under the Haryankas, Shishunagas and Nandas. Of the printed options, Kosala and Avanti were Magadha's main rivals but lost out to it; Kambhoja and Vatsa were minor.

s: Which one of the following is the kingdom of king Dasaratha?
x: King Dasharatha of the Ramayana ruled Kosala from Ayodhya, a city of the Kosala Mahajanapada.

s: Buddha had visited Kaushambi during the reign of
x: The Buddha visited Kaushambi during the reign of Udayana of Vatsa, who became Buddhist under Pindola Bharadvaja (Ghoshitarama vihara).

s: Chand-pradyota was the ruler of which ancient republic?
x: Chanda Pradyota ruled Avanti (a monarchy, though the stem says 'republic'); he fought Vatsa, Magadha and Kosala.

s: Which river is located beside Ayodhya?
x: Ayodhya (Saketa), in the Kosala Mahajanapada, stands on the Sarayu river.

s: What was “Sarthwah”?
x: Sarthavaha (satthavaha) was a caravan/convoy of merchants or its leader, a rich long-distance trader; not a broker, moneylender or pilgrim.

s: ‘Nishka’ in ancient India was known as –
x: In Vedic texts nishka meant gold or a gold ornament (nishka-griva = gold necklace), a prestige object rather than a coin; later it also denoted a gold unit, but never cows or copper/silver coins.

s: In Pali texts, the city is known as:
x: Pali texts use 'nigama' for a town (market town) beside 'nagara' for a large city; the printed key takes Nigam. 'Pur' is the Vedic term for a fortified settlement.

s: Who was the founder of Haryanka dynasty?
x: Bimbisara founded the Haryanka dynasty (NextGen Rocket); Ajatashatru and Udayin were his successors and Nagadasaka the last Haryanka. (PMF notes that some scholars give the founding to Bimbisara's grandfather, but exams key Bimbisara.)

s: Who was a contemporary of Gautama Buddha?
x:
Most books and keys: Bimbisara. Strictly, Ajatashatru (option d) was also a contemporary: he met the Buddha (Bharhut relief), and the Buddha died in his reign (PMF Ancient & Medieval Part 2 p.101).
Bimbisara is the standard answer: he ruled Magadha as a contemporary of the Buddha, and the Buddha visited his court. Udayin and Mahapadma came later.

s: Which Ruler of Magadha was a contemporary of Buddha ?

s: The Prince who was responsible for the death of his father was-
x: Ajatashatru (Kunika, 'Pitruhanta' in Jain texts) imprisoned and starved his father Bimbisara to death. Chandapradyota (Avanti), Prasenjit (Kosala) and Udayana (Vatsa) were not parricides.

s: Jivaka, the famous physician of the time of Mahatma Buddha, was associated with the court of –
x: Jivaka was Bimbisara's royal physician; Bimbisara sent him to Ujjain to treat Pradyota of Avanti for jaundice, so Pradyota was his patient, not his patron.

s: Which initial ruler of Magadha killed his father for enthroning and also was killed by his son for the same reason?
x: Ajatashatru killed his father Bimbisara to take the throne and was himself killed by his son Udayin (Buddhist tradition).

s: Which of the following great ruler founded the "Haryanka Vansh" in ancient Bihar?
o: More than one of the above
x: Bimbisara founded the Haryanka dynasty; Brihadratha founded the earlier legendary dynasty of Magadha (Jarasandha's line) and Ajatashatru was Bimbisara's son.

s: Which Magadha ruler was known as ‘Seniya’?
x: Bimbisara was called Seniya (Shrenika) in Buddhist and Jain texts, from his standing army (sena); Ajatashatru was Kunika.

s: First ruler of Magadha from the Haryanka Dynasty was
x: Bimbisara was the founder and first ruler of the Haryanka dynasty; Ajatashatru was his son and Prasenajit ruled Kosala.

s: Which early ruler of Magadha murdered his father to ascend the throne and , in turn, was murdered by his own son?
x: Ajatashatru murdered his father Bimbisara and was in turn killed by his son Udayin; Udayan was the king of Vatsa.

s: Jivaka, the royal physician of Rajgriha, was the son of the Ganika named as
x: Buddhist tradition (Vinaya, Mahavagga) makes Jivaka the son of the Rajagriha courtesan Salavati; Amrapali was the courtesan of Vaishali.

s: Who was the Physician of Magadh ruler Bimbisara?
x: Jivaka (Jeevaka) was the royal physician of Bimbisara (67th BPSC key: Jeevaka). Shilabhadra was a Nalanda teacher.

s: Who among the following was not a contemporary of the other three?
x: Milinda (Menander), the Indo-Greek king of the 2nd century BCE, lived centuries later; Bimbisara, the Buddha and Prasenjit of Kosala were contemporaries.

s: Bimbisara belonged to the ____ dynasty.
x: Bimbisara belonged to the Haryanka dynasty of Magadha; Pradyota was a dynasty of Avanti.

s: Who defeated and assimilated the Vajjis into the empire of Magadha?
x: Ajatashatru defeated the Vajji confederacy after a 16-year war, using deceit, and annexed Vaishali to Magadha.

s: What was the name of the dynasty of Ajatshatru?
x: Ajatashatru, son and successor of Bimbisara, belonged to the Haryanka dynasty.

s: Which was the capital of Magadha?
x: Girivraja/Rajgriha (Rajgir), ringed by five hills, was Magadha's first capital; Udayin later moved it to Pataliputra. Vaishali was the Vajji (Lichchhavi) capital and Champa the capital of Anga.

s: Which was the first capital of ancient Mahajanapada Magadh?
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Girivraja (Rajgriha)); it is added as option 5.
No printed option is right: Magadha's first capital was Girivraja/Rajgriha (Rajgir). Pataliputra became the capital only under Udayin; Vaishali was the Vajji capital, Champa the capital of Anga, and Anga itself was a separate Mahajanapada. The printed key (Pataliputra) is wrong.

s: Which was the first capital of Magadha?
x: Girivraja/Rajgriha (Rajgir) was Magadha's first capital; Pataliputra came later under Udayin and Vaishali was the Vajji capital.

s: In ancient India, the earliest capital of Magadha kingdom was at
x: Rajgir (Girivraja/Rajgriha) was Magadha's earliest capital; Udayin later shifted the capital to Pataliputra.

s: Where is the highest in the world ‘Vishwa Shanti Stupa’ located in Bihar?
x: The Vishwa Shanti Stupa (World Peace Pagoda), billed as the world's highest, stands on Ratnagiri hill at Rajgir, the old Magadhan capital.

s: By which ruler was Pataliputra chosen as the capital for the first time?
x: Udayin, son of Ajatashatru, shifted the capital from Rajgriha to Pataliputra; Ajatashatru had only fortified Pataligrama, and Kalashoka moved the capital back from Vaishali later.

s: Who among the following kings had founded Pataliputra?
x:
Most books and keys (PMF; APPSC G1 2002): Ajatashatru built Pataliputra. Jain texts and some books (e.g. Lucent) credit Udayin (option d), who founded the city as capital (PMF Ancient & Medieval Part 2 p.101).
Ajatashatru fortified the village of Pataligrama and built the city of Pataliputra as a base against the Vajjis; his son Udayin later made it the capital.

s: Which of the following cities was founded by the king Ajata Satru?
x: Ajatashatru fortified Pataligrama on the Ganga and built the city of Pataliputra. Dhanyakatakam was a Satavahana centre, Nalanda a later university and Lumbini the Buddha's birthplace.

s: Which one of the following was not a capital of Magadhan Empire?
x: Girivraja/Rajgriha and Pataliputra were Magadhan capitals (Vaishali too, briefly, under Shishunaga); Kaushambi was the capital of Vatsa.

s: Bulandibagh was ancient site of :
x: Bulandibagh, with Kumrahar, is an excavated site of ancient Pataliputra (Patna), where the wooden palisade of the Mauryan city was found.

s: Which was the initial capital of Magadha?
x: Magadha's first capital was Girivraja/Rajgriha (Rajgir); Pataliputra came later under Udayin.

s: The remains of which ancient city have been found at the Kumrahar site?
x: Kumrahar (Patna) holds the remains of ancient Pataliputra, including the 80-pillared Mauryan hall.

s: Who founded Pataliputra –
x: Of the options only Udayin fits: Jain texts call him the founder of Pataliputra, and he made it the capital after Ajatashatru had fortified Pataligrama. Ashoka ruled from an existing Pataliputra.

s: Which of the following cities was founded by Ajatashatru?
x: Ajatashatru fortified Pataligrama during the Vajji war and built the city of Pataliputra. Dhanyakataka, Nalanda and Lumbini are unrelated.

s: Which ruler had made Pataliputra the capital of his empire for the first time?
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Udayin); it is added as option 5.
No printed option is right: Udayin (Haryanka) first made Pataliputra the capital of Magadha, moving it from Rajgriha. The Nandas already ruled from there before Chandragupta Maurya, and Ashoka, Chandragupta Vikramaditya and Kanishka came later still. The printed key (Chandragupta Maurya) is wrong.

s: Which dynasty ruled Magadh (Bihar) after Shishunag dynasty ?
o: More than one of the above
x: The Nanda dynasty succeeded the Shishunagas: Mahapadma Nanda killed Mahanandin, the last Shishunaga. The Mauryas followed the Nandas and the Sungas came after the Mauryas.

s: Which dynasty did rule over Magadha after Nanda dynasty?
x: Chandragupta Maurya overthrew Dhana Nanda (c. 321 BCE) and founded the Mauryan dynasty, so the Mauryas followed the Nandas.

s: The expansion of Magadha on Malwa Plateau was under the reign of
x: Shishunaga defeated Avanti (Malwa, capital Ujjayini) and made Avanti and Vatsa part of Magadha; Bimbisara annexed Anga and Ajatashatru Kosala and Vajji.

s: Power of Magadha was extended over the Malwa region during the reign period of –
x: Shishunaga destroyed the power of Avanti (Malwa) and annexed it to Magadha.

s: Which dynasty was ruling over North India at the time of Alexander's invasion?
x: Magadha (North India's leading power) was under the Nandas, led by Dhana Nanda, at the time of Alexander's invasion (326 BCE); the Mauryas came after 321 BCE.

s: Which emperor of Magadha is known as ‘Aparoparashurama’?
x: Mahapadma Nanda, the 'destroyer of all Kshatriyas' (Sarvakshatrantaka), is called a second Parashurama (Aparoparashurama) in the Puranas. Bindusara, Ajatashatru and Kalashoka carry no such epithet.

s: The last emperor of Nanda Dynasty was
x: Dhana Nanda (Agrammes of the Greeks) was the last Nanda king, overthrown by Chandragupta Maurya; Mahapadma was the founder.

s: The epigraphical evidence reveals that under the instructions of a Nanda king, a canal was dug in :
x: Kharavela's Hathigumpha inscription says a Nanda king (Mahapadma) conquered Kalinga, dug a canal there and carried off a Jina image.

s: Nanda clan are followers of which clan?
x: The Nandas succeeded (followed) the Shishunaga dynasty: Haryanka → Shishunaga → Nanda → Maurya.

s: In which century did the first Magadhan Empire rise?
x: The first Magadhan empire rose in the 6th century BC under Bimbisara (Haryanka), a contemporary of the Buddha.

s: Between the sixth and the fourth centuries BCE, ______ became the most powerful mahajanapada.
x: Between the 6th and 4th centuries BCE Magadha became the most powerful Mahajanapada (iron, elephants, fertile land, rivers).

s: Which one of the following was initially the most powerful city-state in India in the 6th century B.C.?
x: Of the four powers, Magadha emerged as the most powerful in the 6th century BC and founded the first empire; Gandhara, Kamboja and Kashi did not.
